slot.brief: verify/compute a vector triple product expression like a×(b×c) or (a×b)×c, possibly testing whether a given identity holds

stem: If vectors $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy $a + b + c = 0$ with $|a| = 3$, $|b| = 4$ and $|c| = 5$, then $|a \times (b \times c)|$ equals
working:
Since $c = -(a + b)$, squaring gives $|c|^2 = |a|^2 + |b|^2 + 2(a \cdot b)$, so $25 = 9 + 16 + 2(a \cdot b) \implies a \cdot b = 0$.
Also $b \times c = b \times (-a - b) = -b \times a - b \times b = a \times b$.
Then $a \times (b \times c) = a \times (a \times b) = (a \cdot b)a - |a|^2 b = -9b$.
Hence $|a \times (b \times c)| = 9|b| = 36$.
